verdicts.id: CITE-1 mechanism: manifest switch plus CITATION.cff subset
verdicts.evidence: Gap is real: schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json:36 has only an optional bare `doi` (additionalProperties false, so no other citation key exists); pages_apps.py:152 renders it as a link in Details; built NucleiSky and CellTracksColab are the only apps with a doi. Verified: no CITATION.cff in any of the six app clones, and raw.githubusercontent.com returns 404 for CITATION.cff on NucleiSky, CellTracksColab, VLab4Mic, GuessTheCondition, the template and Demo (Playground fetch failed, local clone has none). Reference data in the repos is already in three different forms: NucleiSky README has prose plus BibTeX (prose spells 'Hidalgo Cenalmor', BibTeX 'Hidalgo-Cenalmor'); CellTracksColab has a formatted APA-like line; VLab4Mic has BibTeX only. Crossref confirms the NucleiSky, CellTracksColab and VLab4Mic titles, years and author lists (VLab4Mic first author is Martínez, with accent; Crossref has no container-title for the bioRxiv record, so a `journal` field must be author-supplied 'bioRxiv'). Code facts hold: catalogue.resolve, github.raw with a size limit, load_plain_yaml refuses aliases. Counter to the proposal: (1) a 'doi' + 'citation: cff' key pair introduces a deprecation of `doi` and a mutual-exclusion rule for little gain; (2) a rich CFF subset parser (whitelist of person/reference fields, year range, month, status, brace/backslash rejection, 100 KB cap, new $defs, SNAPSHOT_FORMAT bump, a second raw fetch per app) is about 150 lines of new code and a new daily-build failure surface for six apps; (3) strictness means a valid CFF written by a standard tool (type generic or software, preferred-citation without `journal`, date-released) would unlist the whole app over a cosmetic citation error; (4) generating a reference from structured names needs initials/particle logic that the authors' own files disagree on, which is exactly where a wrong citation appears; (5) GitHub's 'Cite this repository' works from a CITATION.cff whether or not the site reads it, so coupling the site to the file is not needed for that benefit.
verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. Site-generated APA text and BibTeX from parsed name fields (initials, 'Del Rosario', 'Gómez-de-Mariscal', 'Johannes Kumra') present a house style as if it were the paper's reference; the prototype was checked against Crossref for only three papers. The 'status: preprint' to 'this preprint' wording and a `journal` value for bioRxiv/arXiv are author claims the site cannot verify. The proposed 'software archive doi' label cannot tell concept from version DOI. A CFF top-level `title`/`authors` (software authors) are not stated by any primary source, so nothing may be pre-filled for authors.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Keep the citation data in the app's labconstrictor-app.yaml as author-typed text, no CFF parsing and no registry calls. Schema, additive only (two optional keys): `citation` (string, 30-600 chars, single line, plain text; the reference exactly as the authors want it copied) and `no_publication` (const true, same style as `installer: const true`). Rules in the schema and one explicit check in validate.py: `citation` requires `doi`; the reference text must contain the doi string (so the copied text always carries the DOI, and a mismatch is a named AppProblem rather than a silent pass); `no_publication` excludes `doi` and `citation`. `doi` keeps its present meaning and is NOT deprecated. Both keys absent stays valid (state 'undeclared', a build warning). No SNAPSHOT_FORMAT bump (the manifest is stored verbatim), no new network call, no new host, no new failure path for the daily build. Authors write the string by copying the publisher's or preprint server's own formatted reference; the site never formats or invents bibliographic data. Authors who also want GitHub's 'Cite this repository' add a CITATION.cff themselves, independent of the site (recommend it in docs/app_manifest.md, do not read it). Optional later, warning-only: compare title and year against the Crossref/DataCite record in submit_app.py.

verdicts.id: CITE-2 rendering: section, states, version, copy buttons
verdicts.evidence: Real in substance: Cite is only a Details row (pages_apps.py:152-153) and only when `doi` exists; page_app (lines 189-208) order is get, about, using, downloads, details. lc.js lcInitCopy (lines 83-92) selects only `.lc-code [data-copy]`, copies the first <code> of the button's parent, and resets the label to 'Copy', so a 'Copy reference' button would need the proposed small change. Partly NOT a gap: the app's version is already separate, as the 'Latest release' row from release_line(app) in details_list, so a version line should reuse release_line, not add a second formatter. check_site.author_strings already scans app['manifest'], so under a manifest-based design no extra scan of app['citation'] is needed. DESIGN.md:38 confirms a link navigates and buttons only copy, a page may have only one filled button outside download tiles (small ghost is fine), and DESIGN.md says add a pattern first. Over-scoped: BibTeX generation (escaping rules for accents, braces, keys), two buttons plus a <details> BibTeX block, a software-archive DOI line, schema.org follow-up and four states with different wording is too much surface for a six-app catalogue.
verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. Lead wording 'the authors ask you to cite' is only safe when the authors wrote the manifest field, which is true in the manifest design but would be a site claim if the text were generated. Showing 'Version X' as the version to cite is misleading because the latest release is not necessarily the version the reader ran, nor the version the paper describes; label it 'Latest release' and say 'name the version you used'. The 'no publication' sentence must be attributed to the authors ('The authors list no publication'), never stated as fact about the world. Generated BibTeX would be a second, unverified rendering of the data.
verdicts.refined_proposal:
New small scripts/lcsite/citation.py (pure functions, all values through text.esc) with one function `block(reference, doi, heading, anchor)` reused by app pages and the home page. App page: `

How to cite

` placed right after using_section and before downloads_table; delete the Cite row from details_list. Three states, each short: (1) paper (citation + doi): 'The authors ask you to cite:' then the reference as plain escaped prose in

, one small-ghost button 'Copy reference', and an action link 'Read the paper' to https://doi.org/{doi}; (2) no_publication: 'The authors list no publication for {name} yet. If you use it, name the app and the version you used and link its repository.' with no button; (3) doi only or neither: 'The authors have not said how to cite {name}.' plus the DOI action link when a doi exists, and a build WARNING naming the app (same 'Not stated' pattern as License); never hide the section silently. Version: one line reusing release_line(app), worded 'Latest release {tag}, {date}. Name the version you used.'; omitted when there is no release. lc.js: let a copy button name its source with data-copy-from= and restore its own original label after 'Copied' (about 4 lines); lc.css: .lc-ref as normal-weight wrapping prose. DESIGN.md gets a 'Citation block' pattern in the same PR, with tests in tests/test_citation.py for each state, escaping of a hostile reference string, and the missing-key failure. Drop BibTeX, the software-archive line, schema.org citation and any APA/BibTeX generation; authors who want BibTeX keep it in their README. Wording of the lead sentences stays an author/maintainer decision.

verdicts.id: CITE-3 LabConstrictor itself: block, footer, duplicate DOI
verdicts.evidence: Verified. grep for 'arXiv' and '2603.10704' across site/, content/, data/, scripts/, overrides/, docs/ finds nothing in the site; the built home page has one zenodo occurrence (the footer). overrides/main.html:100 hard-codes https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20758747, and data/site.yaml:15 holds the same value as links.citation_doi, which no code reads (grep). Primary sources: arXiv API for 2603.10704 returns title 'Packaging Jupyter notebooks as installable desktop apps using LabConstrictor' and five authors in order Iván Hidalgo-Cenalmor, Marcela Xiomara Rivera Pineda, Bruno M. Saraiva, Ricardo Henriques, Guillaume Jacquemet (submitted 2026-03-11). Zenodo record 20758747 is 'LabConstrictor' version 0.0.2, 2026-06-19, concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19074199, it is the latest version of that concept, its creators are the same five people (Zenodo spelling 'Hidalgo Cenalmor, Iván', 'Saraiva, Bruno'), and it carries the related identifier 'describes arXiv:2603.10704'. That last fact supports 'preprint = what to cite, Zenodo = archived software'. The template README (Citation section) reads 'If you use LabConstrictor in your research, please cite the project' followed by the preprint reference, with 'arXiv preprint 2026' and the arXiv DOI, and its badge uses the Zenodo version DOI. The concept DOI page itself returned no JSON through the API (unverifiable by that route), though the version record's relations confirm the concept id. The template is copied into every app (AGENTS.md:28 precedent for the inline template card), so a root CITATION.cff there would be inherited by apps: the reasoning against it is sound.
verdicts.misleading_risk: Low to medium. (a) Writing the reference by hand in site.yaml duplicates the README; author spelling varies across sources (accent and hyphen: README 'Iván', Zenodo 'Hidalgo Cenalmor'), so the string must be copied verbatim from the README line, not reformatted or de-accented. (b) The auditor's rule 'app results: cite the app; discussing LabConstrictor: cite the preprint' is not the authors' stated policy; the README says 'if you use LabConstrictor in your research, please cite the project'. The page must only repeat the README sentence. (c) Showing the version DOI 0.0.2 as 'the software' while the template is at 0.1.15 would imply a version relation that is not true; the concept DOI is the one that stays accurate. (d) No contributions, funding or institutions text may be added from this item.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Do it, smaller: no BibTeX and no software-DOI schema. In data/site.yaml replace links.citation_doi with `citation: {reference: <the README's reference text verbatim, including 'arXiv preprint 2026' and the DOI URL>, doi: 10.48550/arXiv.2603.10704, software_doi: <author choice>}`; validate with the same rule as the app manifest (reference contains the doi). Render with citation.block() as a band with id='cite' and h2 'Cite LabConstrictor' on the home page, lead copied from the README ('If you use LabConstrictor in your research, please cite the project'), 'Copy reference', action link 'Read the preprint', then one lc-small line 'Software archive (Zenodo): doi:...' that is clearly separate. Default software_doi to the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19074199 ('all versions') unless the authors choose the version DOI; this is the one author decision. Footer: replace the hard-coded link in overrides/main.html with an internal link to the home #cite (check_site validates the anchor), keep the label 'Cite LabConstrictor'. Delete the dead key. Add a test that fails the build when site.yaml's reference lacks the doi, and list this entry in AGENTS.md 'Sources of truth' as a deliberate duplicate of the template README. Optional, cheap and recommended: build-time check that the template README's Citation section still contains the same arXiv DOI, so drift stops the build instead of passing silently.

verdicts.id: CITE-4 other repositories: template, initialiser, apps
verdicts.evidence: Real facts verified in the template clone (origin/main): .tools/schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json with README, .tools/python/check_app_manifest.py (104 lines; referenced_paths checks only icon and screenshots; load_schema reads the vendored schema), .tools/docs/app_manifest.md, workflow check_app_manifest.yml, migration v0_1_14_to_v0_1_15 with resources and manifest.yaml. LabConstrictor_streamlit has schemas/README.md ('copy it here and into the template'), manifest_form.py and app_manifest.py that write the manifest. None of the six apps declares citation data and none has a CITATION.cff. Important miss in the proposal: the vendored schema has additionalProperties false, so any app that adds a new manifest key fails its own check_app_manifest CI until its template schema is updated by the sync migration; ordering is template migration released and synced, then app PRs. Also, the claim 'the site must not be pushed before those PRs merge' holds only for the `citation: cff` design (the site would fail apps whose file is missing); with an additive manifest-only design the site change is safe to push first, because apps without the keys simply get the 'not said' state. The NucleiSky draft data in the proposal is correct against Crossref (title, Journal of Cell Science, 2026-08-14 online, doi, eight authors in order, with accents Iván, Adán Olguín-Olguín); Crossref has no volume or pages, only the article id jcs.265152.
verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. The proposal's claim that the CFF subset is validated in the template needs a new validator and CFF example docs in a repo copied to every app, and the 'draft preferred-citation' invites copying registry-derived data into app repos in a form authors have not approved (the three READMEs spell names differently: 'Hidalgo Cenalmor' vs 'Hidalgo-Cenalmor'). Top-level CFF software authors are not stated in any source I checked. The form option 'Yes, I will add a CITATION.cff' presupposes the CFF design. docs/app_manifest.md wording is migration-tied and checked by check_design generic-link rules.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Sequence and scope reduced to what the refined manifest design needs. 1) Site first (additive, safe): schema keys `citation` and `no_publication`, rendering, tests, content/submit.md paragraph. 2) Template (CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor, PR from a fresh branch off origin/main, listed as a separate PR): migration v0_1_15_to_v0_1_16 copies the new schema into .tools/schema/ (same MANAGED_FILES pattern as v0_1_14_to_v0_1_15); no change to check_app_manifest.py (it already validates against the vendored schema, so the contains-doi rule must live in the schema or be a few lines there, decide once); .tools/docs/app_manifest.md gets a short 'How to cite' section (two keys, one example with the reference copied from the paper's own page, and a note that a CITATION.cff is optional and separate). No root CITATION.cff in the template. 3) Streamlit initialiser: only copy the schema; skip the new form field for now (a new app starts as 'not said' and the site warns), revisit if authors forget. 4) App PRs by the authors, after the migration has synced: NucleiSky and CellTracksColab add `citation` text (they already have a formatted reference in the README to copy from), VLab4Mic adds `doi` and `citation` (its README has BibTeX only, so the authors write the formatted line), GuessTheCondition, LabConstrictor_Demo and LabConstrictor-Playground set `no_publication: true` only if the authors confirm there is none. I do not draft app texts or pre-fill software authors. Effort M, not L; the author decision is who confirms 'no publication' for each app and the template version number.
